results: 1. Monocular and binocular visual acuity with refraction
not performed / not available
2. Pupillary examination, including assessment for a relative afferent pupillary defect
pupil size and light reaction: equal and reactive
3. Ocular motility examination in nine diagnostic positions of gaze
adduction in horizontal gaze (each eye): limited adduction of the RIGHT eye that fails to cross the midline, with abducting nystagmus of the left eye on left gaze - mimics an INO
vertical gaze and convergence: normal
4. Cover–uncover and alternate prism-cover tests at near and distance
skew deviation / alternating cover test: no vertical misalignment
5. Assessment of saccades, smooth pursuit, and vestibulo-ocular reflexes
smooth pursuit and saccades: normal
head impulse test: normal - no corrective saccade
6. Measurement of torsion with double Maddox rods
ocular torsion and head tilt: none
7. Hess–Lancaster diplopia chart
not performed / not available
8. Forced-duction testing of the extraocular muscles
forced duction test: restriction consistent with a mechanical cause
9. Orbital and neurologic examination for ptosis, proptosis, and cranial-nerve deficits
cranial nerve examination: limited right eye adduction failing to cross midline, with left abducting nystagmus on left gaze; otherwise normal
ptosis / lid position: none
10. MRI of the brain and orbits with contrast
MRI brain with gadolinium: normal brainstem; subtle medial orbital wall fracture with medial rectus involvement
MRI sella and orbits: subtle MEDIAL ORBITAL WALL FRACTURE with medial rectus involvement; no brainstem pathology
11. Thin-section CT of the orbits and paranasal sinuses
not performed / not available
12. Serum thyroid-stimulating hormone and free thyroxine
TSH / free T4: normal
13. Serum acetylcholine-receptor and MuSK antibodies
acetylcholine receptor, MuSK and LRP4 antibodies: normal
anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies: negative - excludes ocular myasthenia, the commonest cause of pseudo-INO
14. Repetitive nerve stimulation or single-fiber electromyography of an extraocular muscle-related muscle group
repetitive nerve stimulation: normal
single-fibre electromyography: normal
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Right medial rectus entrapment in a medial orbital wall fracture causing mechanical restriction and traumatic pseudo-internuclear ophthalmoplegia (pseudo-INO).

ALTERNATIVE: Internuclear ophthalmoplegia from a small medial longitudinal fasciculus lesion.

ALTERNATIVE: Ocular myasthenia gravis causing pseudo-INO.

ALTERNATIVE: Thyroid eye disease with restrictive medial rectus involvement.
